properties.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
properties.description: A powerful tribute to the victims of the 2001 attacks, built on the original WTC footprints.

properties.name: Wall Street & NYSE
properties.description: The financial heart of the world — home to the New York Stock Exchange since 1817.

properties.name: Battery Park
properties.description: A 25-acre waterfront park with harbor views and the ferry to the Statue of Liberty.

properties.name: The Oculus
properties.description: Santiago Calatrava's iconic transportation hub — a stunning piece of public architecture.

properties.name: Charging Bull
properties.description: Arturo Di Modica's famous bronze sculpture symbolizing financial optimism and strength.

properties.name: South Street Seaport / Pier 17
properties.description: Historic seaport with tall ships, rooftop concerts, and some of NYC's oldest cobblestone streets.

properties.name: Fraunces Tavern
properties.description: A Revolutionary War landmark where George Washington bid farewell to his officers in 1783.

properties.name: Stone Street Historic District
properties.description: NYC's oldest paved street, now a lively outdoor dining corridor lined with 19th-century buildings.

properties.name: Washington Square Park
properties.description: The cultural heart of Greenwich Village — a gathering place for artists, students, and chess players.

properties.name: The Stonewall Inn
properties.description: Birthplace of the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement and a National Monument.

properties.name: Blue Note Jazz Club
properties.description: Legendary jazz venue that has hosted Miles Davis, Dizzy Gillespie, and countless greats since 1981.

properties.name: SoHo Cast Iron District
properties.description: The world's largest collection of cast-iron architecture, now home to galleries and boutiques.

properties.name: Comedy Cellar
properties.description: NYC's most famous comedy club — where legends like Dave Chappelle still drop in unannounced.

properties.name: Meatpacking District
properties.description: A trendy neighborhood of boutiques, rooftop bars, and the cobblestone streets where the High Line begins.

properties.name: Magnolia Bakery (Original)
properties.description: The Bleecker Street bakery that sparked NYC's cupcake craze — as seen on Sex and the City.

properties.name: East River Park
properties.description: Waterfront park with sports fields, running paths, and views of the Williamsburg Bridge.

properties.name: Tenement Museum
properties.description: Step inside 19th-century immigrant apartments and hear the real stories of New York's arrivals.

properties.name: Katz's Delicatessen
properties.description: An NYC institution since 1888 — legendary pastrami sandwiches and the 'I'll have what she's having' table.

properties.name: New Museum
properties.description: The only dedicated contemporary art museum on the Bowery, known for bold and unconventional exhibitions.

properties.name: Mott Street (Chinatown)
properties.description: The main artery of Manhattan Chinatown — packed with dim sum restaurants, herbal shops, and bakeries.

properties.name: Eldridge Street Synagogue
properties.description: A stunning 1887 Moorish synagogue — a landmark of Jewish immigrant life on the Lower East Side.

properties.name: Sara D. Roosevelt Park
properties.description: A beloved community park stretching through the LES, hosting farmers markets and cultural events.

properties.name: The High Line
properties.description: An elevated linear park built on a historic freight rail line, with art installations and great city views.

properties.name: Chelsea Market
properties.description: A vibrant food hall and shopping complex inside the former National Biscuit Company factory.

properties.name: Chelsea Galleries District
properties.description: Over 200 galleries around West 24th–26th Streets — the epicenter of the NYC contemporary art world.

properties.name: Hell's Kitchen Restaurant Row
properties.description: West 46th Street is packed with dozens of restaurants from every cuisine — a favorite pre-theater spot.

properties.name: Intrepid Sea, Air & Space Museum
properties.description: A retired aircraft carrier turned museum, featuring a space shuttle and Cold War submarine.

properties.name: Rubin Museum of Art
properties.description: The world's premier museum of Himalayan art — a hidden gem showcasing Tibetan and Buddhist culture.

properties.name: Chelsea Piers
properties.description: A massive sports and entertainment complex on the Hudson — skating, golf, gymnastics, and more.

properties.name: Times Square
properties.description: The crossroads of the world — neon lights, Broadway marquees, and the famous New Year's Eve ball drop.

properties.name: Rockefeller Center
properties.description: Art Deco complex with the iconic ice rink, Top of the Rock observation deck, and 30 Rock.

properties.name: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
properties.description: Home to Van Gogh's Starry Night, Warhol's soup cans, and one of the world's greatest modern art collections.

properties.name: Grand Central Terminal
properties.description: A Beaux-Arts masterpiece — the celestial ceiling, whispering gallery, and the world's largest train station.

properties.name: Bryant Park
properties.description: A beloved Midtown green space hosting free movies, winter skating, and the NYC Book Festival.

properties.name: Empire State Building
properties.description: NYC's most iconic skyscraper — visit the observatory for a 360° view of all five boroughs.

properties.name: Carnegie Hall
properties.description: The world's most famous concert hall — a National Historic Landmark that has hosted every great musician since 1891.

properties.name: New York Public Library (Main Branch)
properties.description: The Beaux-Arts 'Temple of Knowledge' on 42nd St, guarded by the famous lion statues Patience and Fortitude.

properties.name: Radio City Music Hall
properties.description: The 'Showplace of the Nation' — a spectacular Art Deco interior and home of the Rockettes.

properties.name: United Nations Headquarters
properties.description: The global hub of international diplomacy, sitting on international territory along the East River.

properties.name: Tudor City
properties.description: A 1920s residential enclave with Gothic architecture — a quiet, photogenic escape from Midtown.

properties.name: Stuyvesant Town Community Garden
properties.description: Greenery and community gathering space inside one of NYC's largest residential communities.

properties.name: Chrysler Building
properties.description: The art-deco crown jewel of the Manhattan skyline — still one of the most beautiful buildings ever built.

properties.name: Japan Society
properties.description: A cultural bridge between the US and Japan — exhibitions, films, and performing arts in a serene space.

properties.name: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
properties.description: The world's leading performing arts complex — home to the Met Opera, NY Philharmonic, and NYC Ballet.

properties.name: American Museum of Natural History
properties.description: One of the world's greatest natural history museums — dinosaurs, blue whale, and the Hayden Planetarium.

properties.name: Riverside Park
properties.description: A scenic 4-mile park along the Hudson River with Grant's Tomb and cherry blossom walks.

properties.name: Zabar's
properties.description: An iconic Upper West Side deli and food market since 1934 — the smoked salmon is legendary.

properties.name: New-York Historical Society
properties.description: NYC's oldest museum — 4 million objects tell the full story of New York and American history.

properties.name: Soldiers' & Sailors' Monument
properties.description: A stunning marble Civil War memorial at 89th and Riverside Drive, overlooking the Hudson.

properties.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
properties.description: The largest art museum in the Americas — 2 million works spanning 5,000 years of human creativity.

properties.name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
properties.description: Frank Lloyd Wright's spiral masterpiece houses a world-class collection of modern and contemporary art.

properties.name: Frick Collection
properties.description: A Gilded Age mansion turned museum with Old Masters by Vermeer, Rembrandt, and El Greco.

properties.name: Gracie Mansion
properties.description: The official residence of New York City's mayor — open for public tours in season.

properties.name: Museum Mile (5th Ave)
properties.description: Nine world-class museums stretching from 82nd to 105th Street along Fifth Avenue.

properties.name: Jewish Museum
properties.description: The largest Jewish culture museum in the Western Hemisphere, in a stunning French Gothic mansion.

properties.name: Cooper Hewitt Design Museum
properties.description: The nation's design museum — housed in the Carnegie Mansion, with interactive design exhibits.

properties.name: Columbia University
properties.description: One of the world's top Ivy League universities — the historic Low Plaza is open to visitors.

properties.name: Cathedral of St. John the Divine
properties.description: The largest Gothic cathedral in the world — still under construction after 130 years.

properties.name: Riverside Church
properties.description: A towering interdenominational church known for social justice activism and stunning city views.

properties.name: Hamilton Grange National Memorial
properties.description: The restored home of Founding Father Alexander Hamilton — a free national monument in St. Nicholas Park.

properties.name: Grant's Tomb
properties.description: The largest mausoleum in North America — the final resting place of President Ulysses S. Grant and his wife.

properties.name: Apollo Theater
properties.description: The legendary Harlem stage where James Brown, Ella Fitzgerald, and Michael Jackson launched their careers.

properties.name: Studio Museum in Harlem
properties.description: The premier institution dedicated to artists of African descent and the art of the African diaspora.

properties.name: Marcus Garvey Park
properties.description: Historic Harlem park with the city's only remaining 19th-century fire watchtower and summer concerts.

properties.name: Sylvia's Restaurant
properties.description: The 'Queen of Soul Food' — a Harlem institution since 1962, famous for fried chicken and Sunday gospel brunch.

properties.name: Abyssinian Baptist Church
properties.description: One of the oldest and most influential African American churches in the US, founded in 1808.

properties.name: Strivers' Row (King Model Houses)
properties.description: Magnificent 1890s townhouses where Harlem Renaissance figures like W.C. Handy and Eubie Blake lived.

properties.name: Langston Hughes House
properties.description: The Harlem brownstone where the poet laureate of the Harlem Renaissance lived for the last 20 years of his life.

properties.name: El Museo del Barrio
properties.description: New York's leading Latino cultural institution — celebrating Caribbean and Latin American art and culture.

properties.name: Graffiti Hall of Fame
properties.description: An outdoor gallery on Park Avenue since 1980 — a pilgrimage site for street art lovers worldwide.

properties.name: La Marqueta
properties.description: A historic covered market under the Park Ave viaduct, connecting East Harlem's Latino community since 1936.

properties.name: Thomas Jefferson Park
properties.description: A neighborhood park and community hub along the East River with a public pool and athletic fields.

properties.name: Rao's Restaurant
properties.description: The most impossible reservation in NYC — a tiny, unchanged 1896 red-sauce institution in East Harlem.

properties.name: Union Settlement
properties.description: One of East Harlem's oldest community organizations — providing education and social services since 1895.

properties.name: The Met Cloisters
properties.description: The Metropolitan Museum's medieval branch — a reconstructed 12th-century monastery with unicorn tapestries.

properties.name: Fort Tryon Park
properties.description: A hilltop park with the best views of the Hudson River and New Jersey Palisades, plus beautiful gardens.

properties.name: George Washington Bridge
properties.description: The world's busiest motor vehicle bridge — walk or bike across for spectacular views of the Hudson.

properties.name: Inwood Hill Park
properties.description: Manhattan's last remaining old-growth forest with ancient caves once used by the Lenape people.

properties.name: Dyckman Farmhouse Museum
properties.description: Manhattan's only surviving Dutch Colonial farmhouse, dating to 1784 — a free community museum.

properties.name: Little Red Lighthouse
properties.description: A beloved 1921 lighthouse under the George Washington Bridge — made famous by a classic children's book.

properties.name: Bennett Park
properties.description: The highest natural point in Manhattan — the site of the 1776 Battle of Fort Washington.
